predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a Trump resignation announcement would signal an acute, unscheduled political-leadership crisis. Sudden executive-branch instability raises policy and succession uncertainty, typically triggering a risk-off repricing in broad US equities. The S&P 500 via SPY is the most liquid proxy for US political/macro risk. Absent a genuine confirming catalyst the move is noise; magnitude only reaches the 700bps tradable bar if credible reporting corroborates an imminent announcement.

predictions.reasoning: A credible jump in resignation odds implies US political instability and flight-to-safety demand. Gold is a classic hedge against domestic governance/uncertainty shocks and would likely bid alongside Treasuries while equities fall. GLD is the liquid proxy. The link is weaker and slower than the equity reaction, and gold also responds to rates/dollar, so confidence is modest.

evidence_used: Market question concerns a sudden, unscheduled US presidential leadership change
Baseline probability of such an event is very low; any sharp move would be highly informative
Historical risk-off patterns: political-leadership shocks pressure equities and bid safe havens
SPY and GLD are the most liquid retail-accessible proxies for US political risk
uncertainty_notes: Polymarket probability moves on this market can be driven by thin liquidity and speculative flow rather than real information
The threshold of 700bps is only plausible if genuine corroborating reporting exists; most spikes will be noise
Resignation 'announcement' resolution criterion is loose and could be triggered by ambiguous statements
Equity reaction could be blunted if markets view a succession as orderly (Vance as VP) or even policy-neutral

llm_justification.summary: The market tracks a rare, high-impact US leadership event. A sharp, corroborated rise in resignation odds would most plausibly produce a risk-off move in US equities (SPY down) and a safe-haven bid in gold (GLD up). However, the mapping is noisy: thin-market flow can move Polymarket odds without any real information, so the signal only becomes tradable with credible mainstream corroboration. Confidence is deliberately low and magnitudes wide.
key_assumptions: A sharp odds move reflects new information about leadership instability, not thin-market noise
Markets interpret a potential resignation as destabilizing rather than orderly/neutral
SPY and GLD remain liquid and tradable within the 12h window
failure_modes: The probability spike is isolated speculative flow with no corroboration, and the signal is pure noise
News, if real, is already public and priced, so no further asset move occurs
Markets view succession as orderly/policy-continuous, muting the equity reaction
Gold is weakly exposed and dominated by rate/dollar moves, breaking the safe-haven link
Direction reverses if a resignation is read as reducing policy uncertainty (relief rally)
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
